description: Dance is inherently embodied and thus engages the question of sex and gender in ways both intimate and complex. This course explores the role of gender and the moving body. Surveying both Western theatrical and nonwestern dance traditions, this course traverses a broad cultural landscape to explore the means through which dance communicates aesthetic and gendered meaning and the relation between aesthetic form and social change. We will explore questions of sexuality and changing notions of gender from both biological and social perspectives.
